title: Howes v. Fields
text: The Sixth Circuit’s categorical rule—that imprisonment, questioning in private, and questioning about events in the outside world create a custodial situation for Miranda purposes—is simply wrong. ... The initial step in determining whether a person is in Miranda custody is to ascertain, given “all of the circumstances surrounding the interrogation,” how a suspect would have gauged his freedom of movement. ... However, not all restraints on freedom of movement amount to Miranda custody. ... Thus, service of a prison term, without more, is not enough to constitute Miranda custody.
holding: 囚犯被提出监狱、密室讯问并被问及监外事件，不当然构成 Miranda 拘禁；仍需按“理性人是否感到自由受限”的客观标准逐案判断。
notes: Ellipses omit intervening sentences only; each quoted fragment appears verbatim on the fetched page (syllabus at 565 U.S. 503-505 and opinion at 509-511).
